doc.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996

title: Reaching young audiences, rap and DJs
summary: He wants young people at his gigs, as Art taught, and says jazz players must engage with rap and DJs.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: people. But my problem is all these young people that were young in 1959, it’s 1995 they’re coming to my gigs and wanting me to do 1959. Where are the young people? I want the young people. That’s what I learned from Art. You’ve got to have the young people there. And once you know you’re tapped into the young folks, you know you’re on the right track. So this is the thing I see for the future of the music is that we have an obligation to sit in and deal with the rap, deal with the DJs, deal with all of that because we have the skill and the science and should have the mindset to take whatever comes.
